label: sparse: early original-phase step after a/q/v + v/u/n/j/z prefix, or copied digit 2
explanation: Very sparse feature (0.05% of steps) with low magnitude (max 0.26). Two loose components of about equal mass. (1) Original phase, steps 2-3 only (about 53% of mass): it fires on the third input when the sequence starts with a, q or v followed by v/u/n/j/z/a (e.g. "a n [x]", "q v [k]"). This holds whatever the third token is, but even this tight prefix clause reaches only 13% precision. (2) Copy phase, input digit 2 (about 46% of mass): it fires when 2 is fed back as an input during copying, mostly at late recall positions, but only 1.7% of copy-phase 2 inputs activate, and conditioning on neighboring tokens did not make this precise. The union of the two clauses recalls 98% but has 0.3% precision. It never fires at steps 0-1, at steps 5+ of the original phase, or when copying is off-track (correct=0). The best single predicate (clause 1, dev F1 0.20) is recorded. The feature seems to pick out a narrow region of hidden state that no simple token predicate captures.
